commentBody:
A perfectly fine puzzle.

But not Saturday difficulty by any means.
I'd have been happy with that time on a Tuesday.
This one seemed quite easy for a Saturday after five days of challenging puzzles. And as Sean said, a PESO in the singular is a pretty poor [Tip of Baja]; it’s worth about a dime.
Got a new record for a Saturday today!

Re the Midi:

Anyone else see an issue with the revealer (and the shaded boxes)?

13:05 on a Saturday?  Woah.

Extremely satisfying solve, though.  The wide-openness of the grid was a little intimidating at first.

Easiest Saturday in a long time, felt more like a Wednesday. 

3D "Buttering up?" That one stumped me, good thing the column explained it.
It's remarkably free of trivia and proper nouns.  I was beginning to think I was slipping after struggling with Wed through Friday this week.

Well, we had a nice tough one yesterday from Katie Hoody. This is a nice but not very tough one from Robert Logan. Did Will go SOFTHEARTED, or is he just TEASING by flipping the difficulty levels for this week's themelesses (as he has done before)?
IFSO, I hope we have a devilish Sunday.
Very lovely puzzle. A joy to solve, though I must point out (not in any negative way) that it was solved in about half my usual Saturday time. Very fun nonetheless!

I look forward to a good long challenging Saturday puzzle, one I can settle into and tackle but by bit. When, as happened today, I solve it in 10 minutes, it doesn't mean I have suddenly become a genius. It means you have let me down.

Interesting grid shape. Some things it could represent:

PEACENIKS holding hands in a circle?

RETINA SCANNER focusing on your eyeball?

A  literal HOLE IN THE WALL?

A NONLINEAR ROYAL PAIN? Which I just made up, but seems like the mot juste for certain situations.
With the midterms putting my brain through the wringer, this lighter Saturday puzzle was a welcome reprieve. Enough mental gymnastics to earn my vote, with the fun factor winning by a landslide!
9 Down was very clever.
PB for me. Breezy solve. Good puzzle…maybe better suited on a Wed.

Nice looking grid, decent clues, bright entries, but not Saturday tough.  The great number of long answers and the relative lack of trivia made for lots of footholds, and the grid virtually seemed to fill itself.  I liked noted surname of punk rock for RAMONE.

After plotting out my crossword times for this week, and noting a distinctly exponential look to the curve, I'd extrapolated that today's was going to take me until Tuesday. It did not, and I am *not* going to complain about it, not one bit! Thank you, Logan, for a fun, non-soul-crushing puzzle!
Top quality Saturday

I'm working my way back through the archives and just did a Saturday from January 2011 that took over 40 minutes and required a couple of lookups (don't judge). This one took me less than 7 minutes. I get it that general difficulty is calibrated down these days, and I support making the puzzle more widely accessible, but this feels like it's not even the same game.  A little disappointing. Thank goodness for the archives.

Pretty, pretty, pretty grid with lovely filI, that I had high hopes for but ultimately was disappointed with the challenge as I see many others were. My fastest Saturday probably by a long shot (I can’t see my second) and I wasn’t even power solving. I was wondering if I was just on this constructor’s wavelength (getting HYDROPONICS off the bat  was a big leg up at the top, and RETINASCANNER at the bottom) but clearly that’s the consensus so far, let’s see how that holds up. Maybe the design of this one is just such that once you get something the rest fall in place quickly, but really I just didn’t see anything too tricky except the lovely “butter up”.

I did love the connections in the puzzle, PYLONS and PILEON, and EDEN and UTOPIA. And like I said it was very smoothly constructed. Just not really Saturday material.

Sigh, one of the easiest Saturdays ever (which is not praise).  Just when I was thinking we'd reached the post G.E. era too.  Puzzle was fine I guess, and might have fit well on Tuesday or possibly Wednesday.

XWStats voters concur as "Very Easy".

Although they also seem to list yesterday as "Very Hard", which is not something I noticed.

So..... 🤷‍♂️

With my youngest a toddler and my oldest a teen, I’m well acquainted with 11D. My first gimme was 10A, which we have been seeing a lot of the last few weeks as we tour various high schools for my oldest. (And whew, the public high school process is as convoluted and exhausting as described in the NYT op-ed earlier this week.)

After Friday’s excellent doozy, I too was surprised that this puzzle was over so quickly. But it was still fun and satisfying. And as a silver lining, maybe I’ll get some extra sleep tonight??

Major error. 23D. YEAST is NOT used in a sourdough starter. Sourdough starter consists of flour and water. Thats it. One of the reasons I have and use sourdough starter is to avoid the use of yeast. When I do have the time, I will use yeast as my leavener. Shame on editors for letting  this get through.

I had preemptively felt sorry for whoever had to follow Hoody's masterpiece of yesterday.  That is a tough act to follow.

But this was a fine, solid puzzle in my book, though not as rigorous a workout as I'm accustomed to on Saturday.

On the other hand, I'm kind of exhausted after blue-staring a Tuesday, and working my way back from that.  So, it's all good.

I liked 39D [Drawings of various states], and 3D [Butter up?] was one I'm glad I got on crosses, because I had "butter" very much misinterpreted, and it took me quite a while to understand it even from the crosses.

I stopped listening to rock just before the emergence of The Ramones, so I've never really cared much for them.  Anyone want to enlighten me on their appeal?

I expect some invective over AARGH.

Any Mensa members here?  I'm guessing there might be.  I know one member personally, but I've never heard anything really interesting about the organization.  Do they have a secret handshake?
Really like this puzzle. Thanks! Finally!!

This was the easiest (and fastest) Saturday puzzle I’ve ever done! I don’t think it was me because I’m not that good. Maybe it was because the answers didn’t all involve the latest cultural isms or performers I’ve never heard of.
Two minutes slower than my PB for a Saturday but as others have stated, it measured favorably with my Wednesday average.  After above average times the last couple of days this one flew by…
Never heard anyone call a New Zealand dollar a kiwi

Haven’t even tried a single clue yet, and I am taken back to the Pizza Rebus puzzle.  

It looks so pretty!!

Personal best! 

Let’s go, Brewers!

I really, really wanted "Tombstone setting" to be freezer at 28A, which initially gave me seepSIN, both of which would totally work if only either were correct. Har!  

Alas, 'twas not to be.

My other big wrong answer was inexperienced before SLEEPDEPRIVED  at 11D. Fortunately, I didn't mind giving that one up more quickly, when the crosses persuaded me. 

I liked PEACENIKS at the top and SOFTHEARTED almost in the same position at the bottom. Also, PITA, ARIES, and EPT/INEPT. 

Really liked the grid design. I had a hard time getting going on it I suppose because of those initial mistakes, so it initially felt tough, but then I got on a sourdough roll, got rid of all that nonsense, and finished in half my normal time. I enjoyed it though! Thought it was good fun—though not in that claw your way through it full of head slapping  aha good times.

Whaddya want on yer Tombstone!?
Did anyone else get hydroponics from watching Lost in Space in the 60's?
My fastest Saturday ever was 7-26-25 but this one was close to that.
This puzzle was very difficult until it wasn't. SW ended up being my entry point and I flowed to a 10:35 finish.
A record for me for a Saturday, which happened to be very convenient whilst in a rush today.
A Tuesday as a Saturday? Will, what’s your game? https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=nk3zG_f6DBw
agree with the chorus, shockingly easy but still fun.

this is a puzzle that should give Heart to aspiring solvers - it's not as easy as seasoned players make it out to be - you get better at the crossword the more you do it and learn the ropes.

much like any other learning curve once you become an adept it's easier - that doesn't mean it's Easy - you just get better at it

Fine puzzle Mr. Logan - and a beautiful grid to boot - well done!
Aries Clue makes no sense

Love this puzzle! The grid itself is a thing of beauty. The long answers appeared daunting but then all cheerfully snapped into place. I could almost hear my synapses firing - and then the little dopamine rewards dropping like dog treats as the letters fit and matched.
Awesome job!
Looked hard but was actually way too easy for Saturday
15:12, a Saturday PB for me, well below my average.
Way too easy for a Saturday but fun nonetheless!

Robert Logan, don't feel bad on my account that you didn't have time to add Constructor's Comments. I'm here to solve your puzzle, and there's no need to add anything further. 

As an aside, the link you provided to your earlier puzzle does nothing for me but take me back to today's completed puzzle. Android Games app.

The dive bar put in some miniature plants. It was still a little seedy.

(But I might go there with my buds.)

What a week! According to xwstats, today is the first puzzle that wasn't "Hard" or "Very Hard"

FWIW, I loved Thursday's challenge and definitely do pronounce 'chants' and 'chance' exactly the same. (Frankly, I'm surprised so many took issue with that.)

Followed by Katie Hoody cementing her position as my favorite constructor ever... this was probably the best week of puzzles this year!
This felt uninspired and boring after yesterday's triumph of a puzzle.
Took 60% less time to complete than my average.  Cruised right along without much resistance.  Guessing I am not the only one.  After this challenging week, I don't mind.
That felt very easy. At 12:13, this was the fastest I’ve ever finished a Saturday puzzle.
I know this one! It’s HYDROPONICS! Thanks, Viscera Cleanup Detail!
Sean thought the ARIES clue was the GOAT, but I thought it was MEH.
Someone switched Friday and Saturday again.

Flew through that one. I think the only thing that added difficulty was the grid structure itself, otherwise I don't think this would have made a Saturday.

I won't beat it down though, because I really enjoyed solving it! It was a good, well-executed puzzle, if slightly misplaced...

Fun, but surprisingly easy, especially for a Saturday. I was intimidated by the grid structure at first, but it broke open very quickly. 3 down is a complete mystery to me. Solved it by crosses, but I still can't seem to get it.
an unusually easy Saturday puzzle. Enjoyed it though.

Spunky and fun, but I suppose good things are usually over much too soon. Right off the bat, 1A and 1D had to be PEACENIKS and PYLONS because nothing else would fit. From there, I filled in the top half like a Monday, which made the rest of the puzzle fall in very easily. I finished with a Wednesday time.

I just beat my Tuesday best.

Where to start? It was a fine looking grid, but to put it kindly, the clues lacked sparkle. With so many long entries, there was a real opportunity here for clever wordplay. Instead, we got literal definitions.

“Barrier to entry at a top secret facility” for RETINA SCANNER? How about something like “A real eye opener”? Or instead of clueing HOLE IN THE WALL as “Dive”, maybe “Sundance Kid’s repair project”. 

I don’t know. But when the clue to HAVE A NEED FOR is “require”? And “Mail destinations” lead to HOME ADDRESSES? On a Saturday?? 

I’m actually kind of baffled.
TIL that HYDROPONICS has the same number of letters as AQUACULTURE, my first guess 🤭.
Can I comment on the Midi here? What are PST and TOY STORY T? the T makes no sense in either.

Very grateful to the editors for an easier puzzle after the double gut punch that was Thursday and Friday. 

Also, my best friend became a new dad today, so I appreciated  11 down :)
That was a lot of fun!  Fairly easy for a Saturday, but I'm not complaining.  I think these types help encourage solvers who might be new to Saturday puzzles.

One of the best puzzles of the year, with a clever grid, decipherable clues, a minimum of show-biz content, only one of those detestable mouth sounds (AARGH) and no cartoonish audio representations like KAPOW or BOING which are, IMO, weak constructor cop-outs.
Congratulations, Robert!
That was fun.

Well I feel a bit thick having taken 22 minutes, but for the life of me I could not see PEACENIKS nor make sense of ARIES, despite suspecting the star sign was somehow involved. In case of the former I think my near phobia or pigeons led me to think this was some strange racing breed I had blocked out of consciousness,
Easy can be so much fun and I loved the grid!

That was my fastest ever I think at 22:00 but I’d rather it took longer… want more of a challenge for a Saturday… what am I gonna do with the rest of my morning!?
That said I thought it was a nice puzzle, some good clues, but once I had Ramones and yeast it was sorta paint by numbers. 
Too many Wednesday clues to be a good Saturday.

Senator, I knew Katy Hoody, and let me just say:  You're no Katy Hoody.

Just kidding.

Cool puzzle.

Only because it landed the day after what was by Barry’s standards “a real Friday” doesn’t make this a weak puzzle. 

It’s weak because it took most of us commenting here much less time to complete than our normal Saturday. 

As others have said the same grid could have had tighter cluing.
Anyone else who, like me, confidently slapped down YEN for [Cent : U.S. :: ___ : Japan]?

"With me, surprises are rarely unexpected " to quote the esteemed Detective Clouseau. Too hard or too easy I found the puzzle to be delightful. I found the clueing to be playful. I liked when "home addresses" became evident from a few crossings. (I mean there are plenty of places mail can go!). I liked when soft hearted appeared on the bottom. Loved having 'pylons'  and 'pile on' on opposite sides of the puzzle. I did have primate/same par before private/save par not being a golfer.  And the grid itself was beautiful to look at. Thanks.

Well, I had a grand time racing around the outer track and filling in the donut hole. That was fun. Afterward, I took a closer look and found much to praise. • The grid design (a NYT debut), just lovely, like all of Robert’s Times grids. Want to see a gallery of grid beauty? Look here: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Author/Robert_Logan . • An uber-low 62-word box so cleanly filled, with few arcane answers. Try making one of those sometime. • Freshness. Of the 12 longs framing the grid – eight of them, I repeat, eight, are NYT debut answers. Wow! • Speaking of which, those debuts add distinction to the Times oeuvre. I especially like LOSES LUSTER, ROYAL PAIN, SLEEP DEPRIVED, and SOFT HEARTED, and can’t believe that they have never appeared before. Not to mention the smile I broke into at [Ubiquitous head coverings] for SCALP. A fun romp through a high-quality grid. Thank you for making this and all you put into it, Robert!

It was a lovely grid, which was just clued too gently. My favorite combo was [Dive] HOLE IN THE WALL. And here's the two main members of the Gang taking one. https://youtu.be/PAFUFuNQGuA?si=JfgnTOH_n61j3AM2

The grid design actually made the puzzle far too easy for a Saturday. Almost all of the twelve long entries were simple (for me), and, once filled in, made the rest of the puzzle fall very quickly. Also, the cluing seemed largely Tuesdayish.

Saturday personal best for me, but I don't feel like I earned anything. Editorial mistake today.

You solved a Saturday Crossword in 11:33.

Well, I guess today was easy even by modern standards. As a mere three-year veteran of NYT crosswords, I was hoping I found today’s solve easy because I’ve been working through the year 2016 in the archive. 

Let me tell you, back then the solves were way harder! But in my opinion, maddeningly so. I’m sure that’s the preference of some hardened, masochistic vets who are probably just smarter than me. But I prefer something in between, which is a tough balance to strike. Today was indeed an easy Saturday. (They didn’t have those in 2016).
Thank you for a fun, enjoyable solve!  What a welcome diversion in these fraught times.  Made me smile multiple times :)

Woe is the fate of the puzzle that comes the day after Katie Hoody's!  

JK! 

Today's was like a fresh breeze after a week full of blustery winds which gave us both fits of frustration and deluges of delight.  

A nice, smooth ride...
Found two obvious typos in the Wordplay column today. A bit rushed?

Yesterday was a bit of a wrestling match. Today was barely a thumb war. 

Still, I laughed at a few of the clues and enjoyed solving it. 

I had hope when I first saw the grid but wow that was some gentle cluing today.
This might be the first time completing a Saturday without heading to the column for clues!  A nice confidence boosting Saturday.

I solved this in nearly five minutes less than my average time, but still took twice as long as my best-ever time. 
I was feeling pretty accomplished until I saw all the comments panning the construction. Bummer. 

I don’t think fewer and longer clues lead to easier solves. If you don’t know a couple answers, you’re stumped on a whole section until you get enough crosses. 

So I guess I’m here just to represent the apparent minority who think this was a “just right” Saturday — a beautiful grid with some fresh and challenging clues but enough lifelines to make it enjoyable to solve. 
Each to their own!

It's rare that I can solve a Saturday puzzle without help from Internet or blog.  So I understand the complaints from solvers looking for a stiff challenge and not getting one.  Still, I found today's puzzle loaded with wit and debut answers and it was fun to solve.  Here's some appreciation from an 86-year-old geezer who's not very good at pop culture or computer terminology.

"Butter up"??? 😏

Shofar,  so good!

Did anyone else notice the similarity or repetition between 14D and 46A? Was that just me?

Daunting at first, most of the items that looked challenging fell fairly easily (I blanked on 10A for a minute and started with aquaculture), but I still enjoyed it.

  Re: 45A, one of the key themes in Patriotic Betrayal: The Inside Story of the CIA's Secret Campaign to Enroll American Students in the Crusade Against Communism, by Karen M. Paget, was when and whether leaders in the National Students Association, who had become involved for noble and progressive reasons, would be made "witting", or AWARE that the organization was funded and run by the CIA. I strongly recommend it.

Thanks for a comfortable start to the weekend.
Lovely puzzle, thank you.

Sometimes you're just on the constructor's wavelength. For me, that's a rarity. But today was my day – I felt like I was looking over Robert's shoulder while he put this one together. Huge fun but over so fast. Thanks Robert!

Well it wasn’t super hard but it was fun. I enjoyed working out ROYALPAIN. I started with rightPAIN then went to totalPAIN first as I worked out the crossings. 

I also convinced myself that SCALeS are ubiquitous head coverings. Well they are for fish. Held me up a bit.

NYT Saturday: USA Today edition!

I got 1A within two seconds of opening the puzzle, and that immediately triggered flashbacks from this year’s Valentine’s Day puzzle (also a Saturday), in which 1A clued PEACESIGN as something like “A symbol you can make with two fingers”.

As with the Valentine’s Day cakewalk, today’s puzzle didn’t get any harder after 1A. Come on, NYT…

Well... wasn't particularly easy for me of course, but a good Saturday workout. Did have to look up a couple of things. And... my puzzle find today. A Sunday from April 11, 1999 by Matt Gaffney with the title: "Spring Dream." Reveal in that one was: "D.C. Org dropped from this puzzle or what much of your money is: THEIRS And... some theme answers: HAPLITTERS CHOCOLATEECLA GETAFAHAKE FTFAMILIES SOUVENTAND UPSTADOWNSTA MPACESTATION And there some others. Here's that link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Crossword?date=4/11/1999&h=102a ....
I can't buy a gold star all week and finish Saturday 20min faster than average. The cosmos is misaligned. Cheers!
I learned that Rotten has the same number of letters as RAMONE. And you can’t fit Lionel or Richie in 5 spaces.
“Butter up?”??? Okay.

I loved this one, especially the clever puns. I really enjoyed the lack of arcane proper nouns - I like being educated by crosswords, but not overwhelmed like some do. Thank you for a fun and moderately challenging solve. It was “just right.”
Good Tuesday puzzle.

I'm sure everyone has either already said it or is going to say it in the very near future.  This puzzle was extremely easy for a Saturday and was certainly much easier than yesterday's puzzle.  But I have to admit that I enjoyed it more than yesterday's puzzle -- meaning I may have gone not SOFT HEARTED but soft headed in my old age.  Could I have liked it so much because I am SLEEP DEPRIVED this morning, having awakened at 4:45 a.m. and been unable to get back to sleep?

An easy puzzle doesn't have to be boring -- and the interesting fill made this reasonably engrossing for me. I enjoyed such phrases as ROYAL PAIN, SAVE PAR, LOSES LUSTER, HOLE IN THE WALL and RETINA SCANNER and such words as HYDROPONICS and NONLINEAR.  I really liked the clues for SOFT HEARTED, OVEN, TASTE and LOTTOS.  And though I am not normally a grid-design-noticer, I could not fail to notice the handsome grid.  So for me, this puzzle was as enjoyable as it was easy.  It also played enormously fair, I thought.

More of a Wednesday level of difficulty, but there is something satisfying about filling in those long answers with confidence.  Agree with the column and others that the "butter up" clue was less clever than forced.  When I have to figure out an answer from crosses, when I finally get it and it was a clever clue, I smile and think, gosh people are clever, and then share it with my partner, because clever fun should be shared.  If, after solving, I still need the column to help me understand it, I'm either learning something new (yay!) or I'm thinking, they tried clever and missed.  "Butter up" tried and missed for me.

The inclusion of PEACENIK at 1-Across started an interesting chain of thought for me.
Although there are Hawks to go along with Doves, there are no "Warniks" (that I'm aware of) in our language.

Peacenik, I learned, originated in the early '60s, connected with Beatnik, a term that was coined in the late '50s.  The -nik suffix is used in both Yiddish (see nudnik: a bothersome, annoying individual) and Slavic languages (see especially Sputnik).

It occurred to me that the label PEACENIK was intentionally meant to have Slavic connotations during the Cold War and the "space race" to imply that those who advocated for peace (during the Vietnam War) were pinkos, Communist sympathizers, Soviet stooges.

As for the puzzle itself, I loved the grid (even though it created a Mini in the middle), but there were too many gimmes, IMHO, for a true Saturday puzzle.  However, some of the clues were excellent, especially "Dive" and "Butter up?"
I look forward to spending some time on Saturday but this was over very quickly.

A quibble about 23 across, as a sourdough starter does not have added YEAST. It’s flour and water, and the yeast is naturally occurring, from the flour. 

If you add baker’s yeast, it will dominate the levain, and kill the natural yeast, leaving a bland but usable starter. 

Have seen some odd ideas, like adding apple peels or other fruits the start of the levain, to add more natural yeast. But flour and water have always worked, back to antiquity.

Definitely the easiest puzzle of the week for me but I’m not complaining, it was like a warm hug, with those delicious long spanners. Nice clueing, with the possible exception of Butter up, but ok.
Hunkered down for the second storm in two days. We lost power for most of yesterday, but it’s holding so far today. Apart from a partial collapse of the chicken pen not too much damage so far. Fingers crossed it blows over soon. Where’s our ‘season of mist and mellow fruitfulness’ gone to??

This one made me feel smart when all my long guesses turned out to be correct. But I have to say that didn’t spoil the experience, because it was really quite fun overall. For some reason I really got a kick out of HOME ADDRESSES.
After a week of getting my butt kicked, this was a nice reprieve. Fun puzzle!
After yesterday kicked my jack-or-jenny in all four quadrants (50% over Fri. average time), this was my fastest Saturday yet (Tues./ Wed. time). Weird pair of themelesses.

Are there any other old fogies out there who, before seeing the number of letters,  immediately thought 38 Across was “Ritchie”?

“Tell me how to win … for I haven’t got the clues.”  xD

Somewhere in the back of my mind I had heard of HORSE as a basketball game, but I had to go to MW to make sure. Indeed it is a ball game where you call your shots. 

Seems no one else had a problem with that or else everyone was stressing over ARIES.
Ovid's "our" should surely be NOSTer not NOSTRA?

Looked daunting, but I got a toe-hold and it went pretty fast. 
Did anyone else learn the word HYDROPONICS from "Lost in Space"? They had the "hydroponic garden". Those hours in front of the TV weren't wasted!
Have a great Saturday.

That was so fun. At first glance the layout gave me a lump in my throat but then I slowly realized I was getting lots of fills and the layout became an ally instead of an enemy. In the end it was near a personal best for a Saturday.  That was really enjoyable
The clue about the Pixar movie is about  Dreamworks movie
The grid looked intimidating but the solve came quickly.
This took me about 1 minute longer than my MONDAY average and was my fastest Saturday ever. It was a great, fun puzzle but it certainly belonged earlier in the week.
Wow, I was unsure of virtually every fill except RAMONE, my entire puzzle in gray but somehow it came together in the end.

I was doomed until I wasn't. I had to work from the inside out and had a stark grid for a while, but in the end this one took me about half the time as Friday, and Thursday even. This week has been a tough one, so I was expecting Saturday to be "Final Boss"-level!

Fun puzzle, easier than expected but with some nice twists and turns. Natick-free, and a pretty grid to boot. Thank you!

I'm now bracing for an absolutely brutal Sunday to finish up the week. I get the feeling I'm not out of the woods yet, like a roller coaster with a fake drop at the start.

Contrary to most, I found this one challenging. I had to leave it a while to refresh. But I don’t base challenge on speed of solve, but how it pushes my brain. Thought the cluing was really fun. Enjoyed!

Hard for me to believe this was a Saturday puzzle. I knocked 10 seconds off my average for Saturday. It might even be a PB (love that peanut butter) but I have fudged my statistics. Happy puzzling everyone.
Awesome themeless Wednesday!

I rarely have occasion to say this on a Saturday, but this puzzle was perfectly in my lane. I wouldn't go so far as to call it easy, but I finished under fourteen minutes, which is nearly fourteen minutes under my Saturday average!

This was "whoosh fun" (Lewis, 2026). Let me tell you how whooshy: since 2014, this was within my lowest 3% of Saturday times. But the fun was there, too!

Yesterday after my first pass through the Across clues, I had only one trial answer in the entire top half of the grid. Today was--not that. I did manage to slow myself down through overconfidence. 27A got me started on Boolean logic, so I started off with NOR there, AND across from it, and THEN for "following that..." These created some entertainment when my Downs started arguing with them.

Favorite clue was "butter up high." That felt like an honest-to-goodness Saturday level clue and when I got it on crosses I laughed out loud.
In years of solving (on and off), I’ve only gold starred 3 Saturdays, including today - in 13 minutes! A breeze compared to the last couple of days!
Once I replaced ROTTEN with RAMONE I was on my way.

I’m an Aries, butt this clue was too much of a reach for me. 
Happy weekend all,
M
Definitely hard to start with but once things got going ended up coming together nicely.
i'm glad (and relieved!) that I'm not the only one who found yesterday's really hard compared to todays!

This was my all time best solve time for a Saturday. By several minutes. It is the case that everyone reading this is jumping for joy. 
Please, please calm down. I still want to further improve my time. 
I mean, I don't want to dampen the celebrations, I suppose. 
But I guess I'll say keep them to only a few hours and then return to some modicum of decorum as I face the next hurdle. 
Your worship is appreciated, though. It does not go unnoticed.
This was such an impressive construction. Very dense answers and zero naticks or obscure names
A nice change for me: a Saturday puzzle that was pure fun rather than pure frustration!
I'll add to the chorus of this being an incredibly easy Saturday. I just beat my *Friday* best by almost a full minute.

To add to the discussion, I'm a newbie. I thought this was going to be my first end-of-the-week puzzle completed without lookups, "on my own," gold star, etc. I easily filled in the whole outer circle. Only the center eluded me. I gave up and clicked "Check puzzle." To my surprise, I had spelled ARRGH wrong. Nobody ever taught me to spell AARGH. Once I had that second "A" in place, I could see ARIZONA. Then that whole section opened up for me!! 

I'm glad to see 54D [West Coast univ. holding the record for most chemical elements discovered (16)] CAL mentioned for the second time this month. But commenters might want to know that there are many things that originated in Berkeley other than elements that may never cross their path. Here are some businesses from Berkeley and/or the surrounding Oakland and San Francisco communities: Peet's Coffee, (the beloved) EDYS/Dreyer's ice cream, the Gap, Nolo Law, and, of course, North Face.

poem made from words in today’s puzzle…



a/ what secret moved in the soil
what word from the tree 
intelligence community
hello? hello.
d/ the field weighs low 
following and falling through time
a/ the soft need 
in the soft sleep
home
12:45, which is a very good but not near record Saturday time for me.  Faster than Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday this week.
10:09? Fun puzzle but I'm not that good, so either lucky or way too easy, probably both.
Enjoyable puzzle but very easy for a Saturday - got my 2nd best Saturday time ever.

Cue all the crossword snobs bragging about how easy this was for a Saturday lol

Balancing my contrary feedback from Thursday by coming here today to say I loved this one. Personally thought this was the perfect balance of difficult but doable. I’ve used a few different handles over my years in this forum, but I settled on Anonymous for a couple reasons. One of which being that this is fundamentally an anonymous forum, regardless of what name you choose for yourself. Why? Because user identities are not visibly represented within the system — you get to choose your name every time you write a comment, and there is no way for other commenters to distinguish between one @acjones and another.

Anyhoo, of course solvers of different skill levels are going to have different experiences with any given puzzle! But traditionally (prior to a couple/few years ago), Friday and Saturday NYT puzzles were consistently pretty challenging, even for more experienced solvers. Not that *every* Friday/Saturday puzzle was diabolically hard, but the **average** difficulty level used to be (in my experience) about 2x-3x as hard as the **hardest** puzzle that’s been published within the last ~3 years.
